output.summary: A shrub or small tree found in chaparral canyons and slopes of Southern California, Arizona and the Baja California peninsula. It is long-lived, with dense evergreen foliage, leathery folded leaves and reddish, hairy, sticky fruit.
output.edibilityNote: Cahuilla ate fresh, dried or mashed fruits and boiled flower clusters; Kumeyaay cooked, toasted, ground or infused fruits. Seeds are reportedly inedible.
